thesis: Bet that the honest way to prove engineering ability is to make the artifact itself auditable: spend climx's real machinery (router, GH-Pages deep-link shim, BASE_URL asset helper, mandatory 404 fallback) on three routes, make "no claim without evidence" a non-optional field in a discriminated union so M1 is a compile-time property rather than an editorial promise, and put a `/colofon` route on the page that states exactly what was reused from climx and what was deliberately left behind — so a reader who opens the repo finds the page's claims about itself already checkable.

evidenceModel: Every rendered assertion about a project is a value in `src/content.ts` typed as `Claim = { text: string; evidence: Evidence }`, where `Evidence = {kind:'repo';url} | {kind:'live';url;label} | {kind:'doc';repoUrl;path;value} | {kind:'figure';src;alt;caption;path}`. The `evidence` field is NOT optional, so a claim written without proof fails `tsc --noEmit` — M1 becomes a compile-time property, not an editorial habit. `EvidenceList` is the only component permitted to render a `Claim`, and it always emits the evidence node beside the text: a repo/live claim emits an ``; a doc claim emits the number inline plus its source file path in mono type plus one `` to the repo root; a figure claim emits `

metricSelfEstimates.estimate: 100%. Enforced twice mechanically before it is measured: `evidence` is a non-optional field on `Claim`, so an unevidenced claim fails typecheck, and a Vitest invariant over content.ts asserts every claim's evidence carries a non-empty url/path. On `/` each project renders exactly three assertions (name, status, one-line summary) against one evidence cluster containing the repo link (and the live link for climx); on `/proyectos/:slug` every assertion is a Claim rendered by EvidenceList, which always emits the evidence node beside the text. Residual risk I am naming rather than hiding: prose written directly in JSX — a section subtitle, the profile sentence, a figcaption — is not seen by the type system, so the hand enumeration is the real instrument and the type system is only a strong prior.
metricSelfEstimates.instrument: Enumerate every rendered assertion of fact per route in the DOM under `npm run preview` (production build over dist/), count those with an attached evidence node; plus `npm test` for the content invariant.

metricSelfEstimates.estimate: 5/5. contentGaps: Public-repo status of the five GitHub URLs is unverifiable from disk. The whole evidence model rests on `github.com/Swately/<repo>` resolving for Phyriager, PhyriadFG, Phynned, PHarvard and climx. Only climx's live URL is asserted anywhere I read (its README's «Live at» line). If any repo is private, that project's claims lose their only evidence and the quality veto fails on a broken link — the operator must confirm all five before M-4 closes, and any private repo must be demoted to a no-link entry, which drops M1.

climx's own test count is inconsistent across its sources: README.md says 41 tests, docs/planning/MEASUREMENTS.md records 41/41 (2026-07-28), 50/50 (2026-07-29) and 51/51 (2026-07-31). The page must print one dated figure with its instrument. Resolution needed: either cite the 2026-07-31 row verbatim with its date, or re-run climx's suite for a current number. I am not printing an undated "41 tests".

climx's live Lighthouse numbers (90/100 home, 100/98 municipio) cannot be used. MEASUREMENTS.md records them measured against https://swately.github.io/project-tw/, the pre-rename URL, and E5 states Lighthouse is not installed here, so they cannot be re-measured. The strongest presentation number available for the climx card is therefore excluded and the card leans on bundle/coverage/dataset figures instead.

Three of five project routes have no figure and none can be fabricated (K1). There is no screenshot of climx live, of Phynned's UI, or of PHarvard's board and its seven-of-seven display. All three are minutes of work for the operator and none exists on disk today, so the layout must read as deliberate rather than unfinished with two figures out of five — that asymmetry is a design constraint I am accepting, not solving.

The PhyriadFG diagram I ported is in ENGLISH on a Spanish page (opened first-hand: title «PhyriadFG — external-capture, multi-GPU frame generation», labels Game / Capture / Optical flow / Warp+blend+present / Display, thread letters C/F/P). No Spanish version exists and generating one would be inventing an asset. The Spanish figcaption has to carry the reading, and the language seam stays visible.

Every Spanish string on the page is net-new authoring. src/content.ts is English throughout, ported from documentos_varios/cv.tex, which is also English and stays the source of truth for the underlying facts. Nothing is machine-translatable without a fact check — each string is a translation of something I verified in a README, and a second pass by the operator is the only guard against a translation quietly becoming a new claim.

No favicon, no OG/social image, and no dark-mode support exist in either repo (grepped climx: not one @media, prefers-color-scheme or prefers-reduced-motion rule anywhere in src; public/ has no brand asset, and the portfolio's public/ directory does not exist at all). None is required by M1–M6, so this design does not add them — but a link shared into Slack or LinkedIn will unfurl bare, and a reader on a dark-mode phone gets a white page. Declared, not fixed.

The measured numbers that will appear in /colofon's «Números medidos» table do not exist yet — they are outputs of the M-5 gate run itself. The instrument exists (`npm run build`, `npm test`), so this is a sequencing gap rather than a missing input, but the route cannot be authored with placeholder figures and must be filled last.
weakestPoint: D2's bet is that the reader opens the repo, and nothing on the page can make them. The named workload is a recruiter who decides in twenty seconds on `/` — and `/` alone is served by roughly three of my sixteen new files. The router, the 404 shim, the fallback, the asset helper, the ported test suite and the entire colophon are invisible to that reader unless they choose to go deeper, which means this design spends its whole file budget and all of its payload growth on a second audience it cannot summon. If the reader stops at the home route, I have built with sixteen files what D3 would have built with three, and the extra thirteen bought nothing the metrics reward — M6 is a floor, not a maximand, so the reuse past four resources scores exactly zero, and my own M-3 milestone admits the page is shippable before most of it lands. The concrete technical corollary: my strongest claim, that M1 is a compile-time property, is only true for text that goes through `Claim`. A section subtitle, the profile sentence, a figcaption or a colophon paragraph written straight into JSX is an unevidenced assertion the type system never sees — so the guarantee I am selling is one careless line of prose away from being false, and the real instrument for M1 remains a human enumerating the rendered DOM.
